answer: Each identity registers one cedar grove, locks a 70-credit bond, and seals each resin jar with a key-bound jade tag. The tapper follows a declared wander path, so one tree fills one jar. An auditor re-weighs each jar and checks its jade tag against the log; a short jar, reused tag, or mismatched key burns the bond. The first harvest costs 31 credits; the kth costs 31+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6025 and 1000 fakes cost 3,028,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-resin ring fails because borrowed jars carry another key. An honest agent pays 31 once and reclaims its bond.
